brief: A caddy for next to my kitchen sink: a dispenser that pours out bleach for wiping the counters, plus two bins for sponges.

requirements.evidence: 3-cell cluster (piece:0,0,0;full + 1,0,0 + 1,1,0) with 2 drained bins bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,1,0~hex-bin-full-drain; drained so wet sponges drain
requirements.requirement: caddy with two bins for sponges

requirements.evidence: covered reservoir cell cover:0,0,0;full;top with side hose-barb port:0#0,0#5 as pour spout; no valve/pump/metering part exists in catalog, and configurator knows nothing about chemical compatibility, food safety, or leak-proofing of printed material
requirements.requirement: dispenser that pours bleach for wiping counters

requirements.evidence: No part or prop in catalog is rated for bleach, waterproofing, chemical resistance, or food/cleaning safety; parts are 3D printed in a user-chosen material the configurator does not check. Shape only holds and pours; do not store or dispense bleach in it without a bleach-rated sealed container and process.
requirements.requirement: safe to hold and pour bleach

finish.summary: Small 3-cell caddy: one covered cell as reservoir with a hose-barb side port as pour spout, plus two full-depth drained bins as sponge holders. No sponge/bleach props exist so bins are left empty. Do not use for bleach: no bleach-safe, sealed, metered dispenser exists in the system and material safety is unchecked.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Port plug
parts.use: Blanks a side port you are not using, so a cell that is closed up looks finished and nothing gets in through a hole you left open.

parts.name: Port louvre
parts.use: Vents a closed cell without letting rain in, so a box that has to breathe can still stand outside.

parts.name: Port screen
parts.use: Passes air and keeps insects and debris out, so a cell can breathe through an opening that is still covered.

parts.name: Port hose barb
parts.use: Lands a hose on a cell, so water arrives and leaves through a spigot drawn for it rather than over an edge.

parts.name: Port cable plate
parts.use: Leads cable through a side port on finished holes, so wiring enters a closed cell through something drawn for it and each run has its own way in.

events.text: I see a bleach pourer plus sponge storage — checking what pour hardware fits this system.

parts.name: Blank plug
parts.use: Fills an insert recess you are not using, so the face reads flat and the pocket stays clean.

parts.name: Female socket
parts.use: Seats in a recess and takes a stud, which makes it the bottom of every stacked insert.

parts.name: Male stud
parts.use: Threads through a seated socket and stands proud of the face, so it can carry whatever mounts above it.

parts.name: Foot
parts.use: Snaps onto a stud to give the face something to stand on, so a cell can rest on its cover rather than on its rim.

parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
